assumptions: The only image-observed screen is the sign-in card. Its field examples are treated as presentation hints, not prefilled credentials; sign-in behavior and every recovery screen are proposed.
A minimal synthetic sign-in and guarded demonstration route make account-wide session invalidation observable, without defining a production authentication policy.

A synchronized process-local store with an injectable UTC clock, a private reset-link outbox and a separate in-memory owner-notification sink is sufficient for this demonstration; no actual email delivery is implied.

Use a rolling 3600-second window and private counters for normalized nonexistent identifiers as design choices, while retaining the required five-per-account-per-hour ceiling and identical public responses.
A documented minimal password-input rule will be chosen for the prototype; no password-complexity policy is evidenced.

Approved predecessor REQ-001 through REQ-014 identifiers are used for coverage. The authorized prior-stage reads supplied no citable stage_output locator, so none is invented. No application, dependency manifest, executable test command or implementation result has been verified.

open_questions.context: This proposal uses minimal synthetic sign-in solely to exercise all-session invalidation; the image does not establish an authentication policy.

open_questions.question: Are the email and masked-password examples intended as placeholders, and what responsive fidelity is expected?
open_questions.context: Only their appearance, card structure, labels and relative placement are observed; no pixels, populated values or breakpoints are established.

open_questions.question: Should issued links be inspectable only by tests or also through a local-only demonstrator mechanism?
open_questions.context: The proposal uses a private in-memory owner-directed outbox, never a public confirmation or external delivery.

open_questions.question: Is the proposed rolling-hour window with private nonexistent-identifier accounting acceptable?
open_questions.context: The standard fixes a five-per-account-per-hour limit and identical existing/nonexistent responses, not the algorithm.

open_questions.question: What minimal password-input rule and recovery-page wording should be used?
open_questions.context: Neither a password-complexity rule nor recovery screens are supplied; choices must not weaken the reset constraints.

architecture_summary: Proposed Python 3.12 Flask/Jinja2 server-rendered synthetic password-reset demonstrator, not an existing implementation: browser forms call sign-in and recovery routes backed by one locked, per-app in-memory account/reset/session store and injected UTC clock. A private outbox holds issued links; a distinct in-memory sink records an owner notice for each successful reset. Normalized-address rolling-hour accounting silently suppresses a sixth honored request while every equivalent valid public request has the same neutral redirect and confirmation. Opaque digest-indexed links are valid only before issue time plus 30 minutes, checked and consumed at reset commit under the store lock; the same process-local success transition changes the password hash, increments an account session version checked on every guarded request, and appends the notice before success is reported. The sign-in card is image-observed; all recovery pages, routes and synthetic sign-in behavior are design proposals. State, counters, links and notices are volatile, without durable migrations, real delivery, deployment or production-readiness claims.

hosting.notes: Local-only synthetic demonstrator; no deployment or deployment workflows.

tasks.title: Scaffold isolated Flask state and clock
tasks.description: Establish Python 3.12 runtime/dependency metadata, Flask app factory and Jinja base. Define per-app synthetic accounts with hashed passwords, a locked in-memory store for normalized email keys, timestamps, digest-indexed reset records and session versions, an owner-directed link outbox, a separate owner-notification sink and an injectable aware UTC clock. Configure signed session cookies and account-independent CSRF state for local/test use without tracking secrets; this is not a durable migration.
acceptance_criteria: A Python 3.12 Flask app instance renders a server-side template without a database, real-account service or external notification service.
Two app instances have isolated synthetic accounts, counters, tokens, session versions, outbox and sink; a fake UTC clock can advance each deterministically.
Fixture credentials use password hashes, reset records are indexed by token digest rather than raw token, and synchronization is available for later atomic transitions.

tasks.title: Render sign-in and reset-entry forms
tasks.description: Render the observed sign-in card on GET / and propose GET /forgot-password with a labeled email field, CSRF form state, keyboard-operable controls, field-associated feedback and a return path. Preserve observed copy/order/relative placement without assuming pixels, breakpoints, populated credentials, sign-in behavior or a pictured recovery screen. Prepare the sign-in form for the next slice.
acceptance_criteria: A server-rendered white canvas has one centered outlined card with bold Sign in, labeled Email address and Password fields, a name@example.com hint and masked ******** example, neither exposed as prefilled credentials.
Blue underlined Forgot password? appears immediately below Password; a dark full-width Sign in button follows; gray No account? Contact your administrator. appears beneath the button.
Activating Forgot password? opens a proposed labeled reset-request form with usable focus order and associated validation feedback.

tasks.title: Demonstrate guarded synthetic sessions
tasks.description: Add minimal CSRF-checked POST /sign-in for synthetic credentials and a guarded demonstration view. Put account ID and current account session version into each independently signed Flask cookie; check the version against the store on every authenticated request and clear/reject stale sessions. This tests invalidation rather than specifying a complete sign-in policy.
acceptance_criteria: Two independent clients can sign in to one synthetic account and access a guarded view; invalid credentials create no authenticated session.
After that account's version changes, both clients' next guarded requests are unauthenticated while another account's unchanged session remains usable.
A signed cookie cannot bypass the store version guard; no real identity provider or durable session service is introduced.

tasks.title: Return neutral reset-request responses
tasks.description: Implement CSRF-checked POST /forgot-password and static GET /reset-requested. For syntactically valid addresses always issue the same 303 redirect, location, public headers/cookies and neutral confirmation regardless of account existence or throttle state. Initialize CSRF state independently of lookup. A private service hook, filled by TASK-005, handles issuance without echoing account or token data.
acceptance_criteria: Equivalent valid existing and nonexistent submissions have identical public redirect, destination content and account-dependent headers/cookies, without asserting delivery or exposing an address or token.
Empty or malformed addresses receive the same accessible field error regardless of account existence, before lookup.
The private issuance handoff cannot change the public response; end-to-end issuance is completed in TASK-005.

tasks.title: Enforce rolling-hour issuance ceiling
tasks.description: Fill the private request-service hook under the store lock. For a normalized key at UTC t, discard timestamps <= t minus 3600 seconds, and honor an existing-account issuance only if fewer than five remain; record t when honored. Apply the same private counter policy to nonexistent keys without issuing a link. For eligible existing accounts create a cryptographically random opaque URL-safe bearer token, store its digest/issue/expiry and put its URL only in the owner-directed in-memory test outbox. Suppress the sixth within the hour without a public difference.
acceptance_criteria: An existing account gets five private links for five eligible requests, none for a sixth before the oldest timestamp is one hour old, and another at exactly that boundary; concurrent requests cannot exceed five.
Nonexistent keys get no link; existing, nonexistent, under-limit and throttled equivalent valid requests retain identical public status, redirect, confirmation and account-dependent headers/cookies.
Tokens appear only in the private process-local outbox, not a public response, cookie or ordinary log; there is no external email service.

tasks.title: Present usable or unusable reset links
tasks.description: Propose GET /reset/<token> and a recoverable non-success view. Digest-lookup without consuming the token; render a labeled, CSRF-protected new-password form only if unused and now < issued_at + 30 minutes. Set no-store and no-referrer response policies, omit third-party assets and mask token path segments in logs. Neither recovery view is image-observed.
acceptance_criteria: An unused link before expiry opens a server-rendered password form without consumption; unknown, used and expired links show no success claim and offer a new-request path.
At exactly issue time plus 30 minutes, or after, the form is unavailable; a prior valid GET does not promise success on a later POST.
Token pages use Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, omit third-party assets and do not echo tokens in ordinary page content.

tasks.title: Commit one-use password changes
tasks.description: Implement CSRF-checked POST /reset/<token> and proposed generic GET /reset-complete. Validate a documented minimal password input; under the store lock recheck digest, unused state and strict now < expires_at at commit time. Change only the owning synthetic account's password hash and consume the token in a synchronized transition; structure this transition for TASK-008 session-version and TASK-009 notice effects. On in-process failure restore state and do not claim success.
acceptance_criteria: A valid unused link submitted before 30 minutes changes only its owning account's hashed password, makes the old password invalid and redirects to success only after commit.
At or after exactly 30 minutes, or after prior consumption, GET/POST cannot complete another password change or claim success; concurrent POSTs yield at most one success.
A valid GET followed by a POST at expiry fails; invalid password input has associated feedback and leaves password and token unchanged.

tasks.title: Revoke every prior account session
tasks.description: Extend TASK-007's locked successful-reset transition to increment the owning account session version with password mutation and token consumption. Use TASK-003's version guard on every protected request; clear stale cookies on next access rather than relying on browser-only sign-out.
acceptance_criteria: After a successful reset, at least two distinct previously signed-in clients for the owner, including the resetter if signed in, fail their next guarded requests; an unrelated account remains signed in.
Failed, expired and replayed resets do not change the version or revoke sessions.
Password change, token consumption and version bump form one process-local locked transition.

tasks.title: Record each successful owner notice
tasks.description: Extend the same locked reset-success operation to prepare and append one owner-directed entry to the distinct in-memory notification sink for each committed reset, including a later reset via a fresh link. On an in-process sink failure restore state or abort without reporting success. A sink record does not prove external or durable delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Two distinct successful resets for one synthetic account produce two separate owner-addressed sink records, one for each success.
Expired, unknown, invalid-input, replayed and losing concurrent POST attempts produce no notification or false success.
A simulated in-process sink failure cannot leave a claimed successful password change without its record; no external notification service is added.

tasks.title: Test sign-in, parity and hourly edges
tasks.description: Add pytest/Flask-client checks for the observed card and proposed reset entry, response parity for existing/nonexistent normalized keys and throttled states, and the fifth/sixth/rolling-hour boundaries using the fake clock and private outbox. Compare public response surfaces, not just copy.
acceptance_criteria: Pytest checks observed card copy, controls and relative order and that Forgot password? opens a request form; no unseen recovery pixels or pictured authentication policy are asserted.

For equivalent existing/nonexistent requests, compare status, Location, redirect destination content and account-dependent headers/cookies below and at/above the limit; inspect the private outbox separately for no disclosure.

At fixed t0, the first five requests issue five existing-account links, a sixth at t0+3599 seconds issues none, and a request at t0+3600 seconds is eligible with unchanged public response; malformed inputs have account-independent errors.

tasks.title: Test reset boundaries and effects
tasks.description: Add isolated pytest cases with a fake aware UTC clock and multiple Flask clients for valid password changes, exact expiry, replay/concurrency, all-session invalidation, per-success owner notices, non-success UI and token response protections after TASK-009 integrates the effects.
acceptance_criteria: Separate links test successful completion one microsecond before issue+30 minutes, rejection exactly at and after it, and failure of a POST whose preceding GET was valid but whose commit time is expired.
Used or concurrently replayed links cannot change a password again or append another notice; invalid and expired attempts preserve password, version and notice count.

After a valid reset, two or more prior owner sessions are rejected while another account remains signed in; two distinct successful resets leave two owner-directed sink records. Run pytest on Python 3.12 and report actual outcomes.

tasks.title: Document limitations and inspect delivery scope
tasks.description: Document local setup, pytest execution, synthetic fixtures, private link inspection, volatile process-local counters/tokens/session versions/outbox/notification sink, process restart and multi-worker limitations, lack of real delivery and incomplete production security. Review final changes and execution record for deployment or new deployment workflows without adding such infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Project documentation identifies synthetic-account, in-memory and notification-delivery production limits without claiming production readiness.
Final deliverable review confirms no deployment occurred and no deployment workflow was added; local testing is not deployment.
No production service, durable migration, deployment configuration, workflow or hosted environment is introduced by this documentation/review task.
